Every package and file of the repository with its types and functions, and the first sentence of each one's doc comment.
Unexported (lowercase) names are internal to their package. Test files are listed with their test functions.
The [architecture chapters](../architecture/overview.md) explain how these fit together.

## `internal/problems` {#internal-problems}

Package problems keeps the platform's own warnings and errors for the Problems page: a slog handler passes every record on to the real log and also queues warnings and errors; a Recorder stores them, folding repeats of the same problem into one row with a count.

| `barrios` | func | barrios puts every system in a barrio: the one its app declares; else, for an app that calls other apps or is called by them, the barrio of the apps it talks to most (label propagation, weighted by calls per minute where traces measured them); else the centre. |
| `(*builder) traced` | method | traced adds the numbers measured from traces to the edges they belong to, and the calls only traces know about (to a service nobody declared, or outside the cluster) as edges of their own. |
| `(*builder) resolve` | method | resolve finds the node a collector name stands for: "app/service" (what observe names services), "user" (a call from outside, the internet), a cluster address (api.wellness.svc.cluster.local:8000, api.wellness), a short name in the caller's system (api:8000), or a database the caller's app runs (postgresql, redis). |
| `systemKind` | func | systemKind is the kind of system a catalog entry belongs to. |
| `builder` | struct | builder collects nodes, systems and edges by ID while the graph is made. |
| `(*builder) system` | method | system adds s, keeping the first one seen for an ID (apps come first, so an app's system keeps its kind and repo). |
| `(*builder) node` | method | node is the node with id, added in system when new. |
| `(*builder) edge` | method | edge records from calling to, merging what each source says about it. |
| `(*builder) edgesFrom` | method | edgesFrom lists the edges leaving id. |
| `(*builder) dropLoneInfrastructure` | method | dropLoneInfrastructure removes cluster plumbing nobody outside it calls: ingress controllers, cert-manager and the like are noise on the map unless an app depends on them. |
| `(*builder) health` | method | health attaches each service's latest uptime checks: up when every latest check passed. |
| `contains` | func | contains reports whether list has s. |

## `internal/uptime` {#internal-uptime}

Package uptime checks every app's services once a minute and keeps the results: whether each answered, how fast, and when it was down.

### `internal/uptime/uptime.go`

<small>545 lines</small>

| Name | Kind | Summary |
|---|---|---|
| `Target` | struct | Target is one check: a URL to GET, or a host:port to connect to. |
| `Targets` | func | Targets lists the checks for a set of apps. |
| `Checker` | struct | Checker runs single checks. |
| `NewChecker` | func | NewChecker returns a Checker that does not follow redirects (a redirect, say to a login page, means the service answered) and gives each check timeout to complete. |
| `(*Checker) Check` | method | Check runs one check. |
| `shortError` | func | shortError keeps the useful end of an error (Go wraps URLs and addresses around the cause). |
| `Recorder` | interface | Recorder is what the prober stores results in (the store in production). |
| `Prober` | struct | Prober checks every target once per Interval and records the results. |
| `checkState` | struct |  |
| `change` | struct | change is an outage that started or ended, for the round's emails. |
| `key` | func | key identifies one check: app, service and kind (public or internal). |
| `(*Prober) Run` | method | Run checks until ctx is done. |
| `(*Prober) Round` | method | Round checks every target once, records the results and updates outages. |
| `(*Prober) loadAnswered` | method | loadAnswered learns which checks have ever succeeded, so a restart does not treat a long-working domain as new. |
| `(*Prober) markDNSPending` | method | markDNSPending rewrites the error of a public check that has never answered and fails its DNS lookup, for its first DNSGrace: a new domain whose record is still spreading. |
| `(*Prober) notifyChanges` | method | notifyChanges sends one email per app for the outages that started, and one for those that ended, this round. |
| `checkName` | func | checkName is a check as emails and pages name it. |
| `joinAnd` | func | joinAnd lists names as "a and b and c", one translatable pair at a time. |
| `outageMessage` | func | outageMessage is the email that says an app's checks went down, since when and what they answered. |
| `recoveryMessage` | func | recoveryMessage is the email that says the checks are back, and how long they were down. |
| `humanDuration` | func | humanDuration is a duration in words ("under a minute", "12 min", "2 h 5 min"). |
| `(*Prober) observe` | method | observe updates a target's streak, its metrics, and opens or closes its outage. |
| `Register` | func | Register adds the uptime metrics to a Prometheus registry (the controller-runtime one, served on METRICS_ADDR). |
